newsitem.title: CANADA: Methanex says prices firm, inventories lean.
newsitem.headline: Methanex says prices firm, inventories lean.

text.p: Methanex Corp, the world's biggest methanol producer, said on Thursday that prices of the chemical were up a "bit" in the fourth quarter over the third quarter, while inventories industrywide were fairly low.
Chief executive Pierre Choquette told a conference call that Methanex's third-quarter sales volume of 1.5 million tonnes was up 16 percent over the same period of 1995.

The company has about 25 days of supply on hand. "Our inventories are tight but we have been able to meet all our customer requirements," he said. Methanol prices currently "are a little bit above" the third quarter, he said.
"We expect to see a slight movement up in prices... Inventories are very, very low right now," Choquette said.
He discounted talk of impending price weakness, saying outages that have plagued other producers this year have prevented softening.

Choquette said the company's sales growth appeared to be "at least twice that of the market overall." Methanex's global average price for methanol in the third quarter was US$0.45 a gallon, up from US$0.42 a gallon in the second quarter. Methanex reported earnings of US$0.13 a share in the third quarter, up from US$0.06 in the same period a year earlier.
All the company's plants will operate at maximum rates in the fourth quarter, Choquette said.

Methanol is made from natural gas and is used in a wide array of products including formaldehyde, paint, resins, building products and as an additive in clean-burning gasoline. Demand for the chemical is closely linked to the economic cycle.
"We see good, healthy demand in all sectors," Choquette said.
Construction of Methanex's second plant in Chile is on track for completion and start up at the end of the year.

Methanex recently announced plans to build a third plant in Chile. Choquette said when it is complete the company will have three million tonnes of capacity there which will return more than the company's cost of capital when methanol prices are at midcycle around US$150 a tonne.

With US$347 million in cash on hand and operations generating about US$60 million in cash per quarter, Methanex is also looking at other "strategic investments" in the methanol business, Choquette said.
"We still have substantial financial capability to look at other major transactions and we are pursuing these," he said.

The company's natural gas supply contracts there dwindle until they expire in 2003 and 2005. While they might be renewed, Methanex is planning on the assumption it may not have access to long-term low-cost gas in New Zealand, Choquette said.
The company overall is making progress on driving its costs down and its production costs are now four to five percent below year ago levels.
A Methanex spokesman said the company estimates its share of the world merchant methanol market at about 34 to 35 percent, up from 33 percent last year.
